title: Transfer of coefficient equations to every positive-degree Proj chart
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $L$ invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], $S$ its section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], $d>0$, $s\in S_d$, and $U$ open with $s|_U$ a free generator [def-sc-local-free-generator]. Let $\rho:S_{(s)}\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ring map satisfying $\rho(\xi/s^n)s^n|_U=\xi|_U$ for every $n$ and $\xi\in S_{nd}$. Let $q:U\to\operatorname{Spec}S_{(s)}$ induce $\rho$ on global sections under the canonical spectrum and open-subscheme section identifications [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Set $g=q\circ\iota_s:U\to\operatorname{Proj}S$ [def-pc-proj]. For every $e>0$, $t\in S_e$, $n\geq0$, and $\xi\in S_{ne}$, on the ambient image $W\subseteq X$ of $g^{-1}D_+(t)$ one has $g^\sharp(\xi/t^n)(t^n)|_W=\xi|_W$. This theorem verifies a given affine map; it asserts no existence of $q$ or $\rho$.

source.place: Tags 01N8 (local quotient construction and comparison) and 01NK (different positive degrees)

proof.text: Choose a local basis z of L on U, writing s=b z^d and t=c z^e. The free-generator hypothesis makes b a unit. The assumed equations identify rho(a/s^k) with the coefficient of a divided by b^k. By the Proj chart description, D_+(s) intersect D_+(t) is the basic open of t^d/s^e in Spec S_(s). Its preimage under q is the unit locus of c^d/b^e, equivalently that of c. This follows from the affine morphism correspondence and its basic-open preimage formula.

proof.text: On this intersection use the degree-zero fraction identity xi/t^n = (xi t^{n(d-1)}/s^{ne}) / (t^d/s^e)^n. The numerator on the right has degree ned. The ring-map equations and localization give its pullback as the coefficient of xi divided by c^n, because b^{ne} and c^{n(d-1)} cancel. Multiplication by t^n gives xi. These are local equations of module sections and hence glue. The same identity handles n=0. Empty intersections give equality of unique sections. The unit criterion for powers holds without reducedness.
